title: Liquify Tool in Photoshop: Non-destructive clean-up of clothing edges (Day 15 of 30 Days of Photoshop)
summary: In this PHLEARN tutorial, Aaron Nace demonstrates a practical, non-destructive workflow for using Photoshop's Liquify tool to clean and tighten lines on fashion imagery. The lesson starts with converting the layer to a Smart Object to enable non-destructive edits, then walks through the Forward Warp tool for shaping clothing, the Reconstruct brush as a controlled undo, and the more specialized tools (Pucker, Bloat, Pluck/Blow). A Freeze Mask is introduced to restrict edits, and the session concludes with a strong emphasis on using Generative Fill to remove wrinkles and refine texture, followed by a before/after comparison and guidance on applying these techniques to fashion shoots.
topics: Brush size, pressure, and density controls
Pluck, Blow, and related liquify tools (less frequently used)
Clothing edge refinement in fashion imagery
Background distortion awareness during liquify edits

sections.title: Introduction and Smart Object Preparation
sections.description: Introduction to the day’s focus on liquify for fashion edits. Aaron outlines non-destructive editing by converting the layer to a Smart Object (Filter > Convert for Smart Filters) and previews the goal: cleaner lines on clothing to improve the overall image.

sections.title: Forward Warp Tool: Basic Use and Controls
concepts: Zoom and practice on clothing edges
sections.description: Explains how to access the Liquify filter and demonstrates the Forward Warp tool: clicking and dragging to push/pull areas, using brush size adjustments with [ and ], and leveraging non-destructive edits by zooming in and testing changes while preserving background integrity.

sections.title: Reconstruct Tool: Undo-like Refinement
concepts: Applying edits to pockets and seams
sections.description: Introduces the Reconstruct tool as an on-screen brush-based undo, enabling restoration to a prior state if changes go too far. Demonstrates refining pockets and edges while noting background interaction and the goal of minimizing unintended background shifts.

sections.title: Additional Liquify Tools and Practical Guidance
concepts: Preference for Forward Warp in many cases
sections.description: Reviews other liquify options (pucker, bloat, and related tools) and discusses practical usage. Emphasizes that while these tools exist, the Forward Warp tool often provides more reliable control for clothing edits and line clean-up.

sections.title: Freeze Mask and Reconstruct Emphasis
concepts: Masking areas to avoid affecting them
sections.description: Shows how to paint a Freeze Mask to protect specific areas, then uses Reconstruct again with a suggested 74% amount to balance edits. Emphasizes keeping edits non-destructive by testing the Smart Object on/off for comparison.

sections.title: Generative Fill: Wrinkle Removal and Refinement
sections.description: Highlights the AI-assisted wrinkle removal workflow: paint over wrinkles with the selection brush, then use Generative Fill to remove them. Demonstrates how the result improves exterior lines and interiors, followed by a before/after comparison to illustrate impact.

sections.title: Takeaways and Series Teaser
sections.description: Concludes with practical takeaways for fashion imagery, reiterating the power of liquify for cleaning exterior lines and edges. Ends with a teaser for the next day in the series, focusing on Smart Objects.
